subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After authorization ordering is fixed, should plugin-runtime callers be categorically denied patch access to legacy ownerless session rows without an automatic ownership migration?
rationale: The ordering defect is mechanical, but code and existing contracts do not establish the intended upgrade authority for rows created before plugin ownership was persisted.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject ownerless rows and require an operator or non-plugin client for recovery, with explicit upgrade proof.

options.title: Migrate ownership
options.body: Add a doctor or migration owner that establishes canonical ownership before runtime enforcement.

options.title: Delay enforcement
options.body: Temporarily preserve ownerless access until a deprecation and migration plan is approved.

recommendation.title: Fail closed
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows and require an operator or non-plugin client for recovery, with explicit upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest ownership of Gateway session lifecycle and control behavior, including archive and delete semantics.
